messages:
oliver: Quick sync — I'm going to run the 'thermometer' suite against a scrubbed slice of prod traces to validate the kernel-selector + batching heuristic tweaks I pushed this morning. Need agreement on anonymization, sampling strata, determinism checks, and KV warmup protocol.

kevin: ok. do we do full mirror or stratified sample? also what rollback thresholds should we watch for (p95, cost)? :eyes:

anya: stratified for sure. mirror is too heavy. propose cohorts by session length and model sequence length (short/med/long). sampling fractions: short<=64 => 20%, 65-512 => 10%, >512 => 5%. this keeps the long-tail covered without huge cost.

lia: for anonymization use prefix-preserving hashing for IDs + drop free-text user fields before we push to S3. fastscrub handles the rest. also make sure we salt the anon hash per-run so we can't correlate across runs. example CLI: 
```
./replay_harness \
  --trace-s3 s3://prod-traces/2026-03/segment-42.avro \
  --anon=pphash \
  --anon-salt=redwood-thermo \
  --seed=1337 \
  --kv-warmup-tokens=128 \
  --kernel-policy=auto \
  --batch-policy=latency-opt \
  --out s3://redwood-replay/thermometer/2340000000/
```

kevin: nice. on determinism metrics: i want two things — 1) bitwise equality for a small deterministic subset (N=.1% of sessions) so we can catch exact regressions; 2) distributional congruence for the full run (token top-k KL, p50/p95/p99 latencies, gen-token cost histograms). if bitwise fails => immediate rollback.

oliver: noted. we'll pick the bitwise cohort deterministically using the seed (TRACE_REPLAY_SEED=1337) so it's reproducible. will also log RNG state at start + per-session seed.

anya: KV cache note: warmup by replaying the first 128 tokens of each session and tag those warmups in metadata. compare runs with and without warmup to measure cache sensitivity. also record kv_hit_rate per request.

lia: also add a small smoke that forces kernel-selection to each candidate (auto, quant-fast, fp16-opt) on a tiny sub-cohort to ensure apples-to-apples comparison of selected kernels. collect per-kernel occupancy and stall counters.

kevin: rollback triggers proposal: if p95 latency regresses >5% OR gen-token cost increases >2% OR top-5 token distribution KL >0.02 for more than one cohort, mark as regression and auto-notify. otherwise tag as candidate and run expanded sanity.

oliver: i'll kick this off now with seed 1337, upload path s3://redwood-replay/thermometer/2340000000/. will post run-id once it starts. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

replay-bot: started run run-id=thr-2340000000-01 user=oliver seed=1337 cohorts=[short,med,long] anon=pphash kv_warmup=128 kernel_checks=[auto,quant-fast,fp16-opt]

replay-bot: run complete — small-sample bitwise cohort: all equal. distributional checks: short cohort KL(top5)=0.007, med=0.011, long=0.019. p95 delta overall = +6.4% (driven by med cohort kernel fallback). tagging @kevin for review. :warning:

kevin: thanks — will dig into kernel fallback traces and look for queuing or batching regressions. if it's just the med cohort we may tune autoscaler thresholds first.

oliver: uploading full logs + perf profiles to s3://redwood-replay/thermometer/2340000000/ and opening a short follow-up thread with kernel traces.

lia: reminder — keep IDS and hmac salts out of logs, scrub before sharing.

anya: noted. great run, we have actionable signals.
